bill_of_lading.notify_party: Hanbit Refining Co., Ltd., Ulsan, Republic of Korea

commercial_invoice.payment_terms: Irrevocable L/C at sight (90% provisional / 10% on final QP)
commercial_invoice.pricing_basis: Platts Dated Brent (QP mean over 5 quotations from B/L date) + Murban grade differential

insurance.policy_type: Marine cargo all risks + war risk (energy)

trade_economics.note: Exporter contracted the cargo at ~USD 77/bbl earlier in the cycle versus the CIF Ulsan invoice of USD 96.5/bbl; the war premium is embedded margin. Profit (= invoice 57,900,000 - COGS 46,200,000 = 11,700,000) funds the RWA discount.

market.source: calibrated to ICE Brent June 2026 (Strait of Hormuz conflict, +43% y/y)

shipment_events.description: 600,000 bbl Murban crude loaded ex Universal Terminal shore tanks onto MT Strait Voyager.
Laden tanker northbound to Ulsan on schedule.

macro_risk_events.description: US-Iran conflict and threatened closure of the Strait of Hormuz are the dominant driver of crude prices; cargo loads ex-Singapore (post-Hormuz), reducing transit war exposure but not benchmark price risk.
Brent near USD 95/bbl, +43% y/y, with falling US inventories; large daily swings mean RWA collateral valuation needs a volatility haircut on the war premium.
Energy-driven inflation pressuring KRW; buyer pays in USD under L/C, so direct FX exposure to the pool is limited.
